cutouts.label: Red Wedge
cutouts.creator: El Lissitzky (1890–1941)
cutouts.license: This photographic reproduction is therefore also considered to be in the public domain in the United States.
cutouts.keep: Cut the red wedge — single clean triangle driving into the white circle; poster text stays out of the cut.
cutouts.tag_reason: The red wedge's diagonal thrust into the white circle, set against hard black and cream, delivers a feeling of forceful attack and forward momentum — a strike already in motion, with the boldness of the composition inviting admiration.

cutouts.label: Proun 99
cutouts.creator: El Lissitzky (1890–1941)
cutouts.license: This photographic reproduction is therefore also considered to be in the public domain in the United States.
cutouts.keep: Cut the faceted composite object upper left — black/grey/white planes, clean edges; the red arc and hatched fan stay out.
cutouts.tag_reason: The faceted black-grey-white form hangs impossibly in flat grey space, steadied by a thin red arc and a hatched fan converging to a point, so it delivers quiet wonder at an engineered impossibility rather than agitation — a calm, hovering strangeness that invites long looking.

cutouts.label: Konstruktivizm cover
cutouts.creator: Aleksei Gan
cutouts.license: This work is ineligible for copyright and therefore in the public domain because it consists entirely of information that is common property and contains no original authorship.
cutouts.keep: Cut the black КОНСТРУКТИВИЗМ bar — single clean rectangle; red name lettering stays out.
cutouts.tag_reason: The stark red name over the heavy black bar, unadorned on worn cream paper, delivers the calm certainty of a movement announcing itself — a declaration that trusts its own minimal typography to carry the weight.

cutouts.label: ROSTA poster: Want it? Join
cutouts.creator: Mayakovsky, Vladimir
cutouts.license: This work is in the public domain in its country of origin and other countries and areas where the copyright term is the author's life plus 70 years or fewer. This work is in the public domain in the United States because it was published (or registered with the U.S. Copyright Office) before January 1, 1930.
cutouts.keep: Cut the red worker eating corn, bottom left — solid red figure on cream, clean edge; poster text stays out.
cutouts.tag_reason: The grotesque cold-monster and hunger-skeleton loom as threats in the top panels while the solid red workers eat corn and drink with satisfaction below, delivering a combative rallying energy — the enemies are the monsters, never the workers, who are the poster's heroes.

cutouts.label: VKhUTEMAS cover
cutouts.creator: El Lissitzky (1890–1941)
cutouts.license: This work is in the public domain in the United States because it was published (or registered with the U.S. Copyright Office) before January 1, 1931.
cutouts.keep: Cut the hand with the compass — solid photographic form on graph paper; diagonal typography stays out.
cutouts.tag_reason: The hand grips the compass firmly and holds it poised over graph paper while the bold red-and-black type slashes diagonally across the frame, delivering the alert focus of a worker about to draw — readiness and craft, not a passive portrait.

snippets.name: beam-frame
snippets.author: Kit coder (original code)
snippets.why: The poster frame as scaffolding — red and black bars along the edges only, leaving the centre completely clear for the poem.

snippets.name: diagonal-thrust
snippets.author: Kit coder (original code)
snippets.why: The diagonal thrust of constructivist composition — everything leans upward and forward along the same 45° axis, never drifting sideways.

snippets.name: beam-and-disc
snippets.author: Kit coder (original code)
snippets.why: The beam-and-disc motif of Rodchenko and Lissitzky — a red diagonal girder capped by a black circle, the movement's industrial geometry reduced to two shapes.
